title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Partial replacement of Zr4+ by Ce4+ in Cu/UiO-66 does not raise the methanol yield from CO2 hydrogenation but can increase methanol selectivity; oxygen spillover between Ce4+ and Cu0 is invoked to explain a loss of Cu0 sites and a lower yield than Cu/UiO-66(Zr).
explanation: Łamacz replaced about half of the Zr in Zr6 nodes with Ce. Ce sites are described as adsorbing CO2 as carbonate that is hydrogenated onward to formate and methanol, accounting for higher selectivity without a higher yield.
scope: Cu-loaded mixed Ce/Zr UiO-66 for thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methanol.
conditions: 200 °C, 1.8 MPa, H2/CO2 = 3:1, 25 h; reported yield 397 μmolMeOH gCu−1 h−1 and 56% selectivity.
caveats: The oxygen-spillover explanation is the review’s reading of that study and is specific to Cu on Ce/Zr nodes.
